definitions.explanation: The second-in-command within an organization or department. Ranks directly below the head (長) and acts as a substitute or assistant. Common in government agencies, corporations, and other organizations.

examples.japanese: {田中|たなか}さんが{次長|じちょう}に{昇進|しょうしん}した。
examples.english: Tanaka was promoted to deputy director.

examples.japanese: {部長|ぶちょう}が{不在|ふざい}のときは{次長|じちょう}が{代行|だいこう}する。
examples.english: When the department head is absent, the deputy director acts in their place.

examples.japanese: {次長|じちょう}として{長年|ながねん}{組織|そしき}を{支|ささ}えてきた{功績|こうせき}が{認|みと}められた。
examples.english: His long years of service supporting the organization as deputy director were recognized.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {次|じ} (next, secondary) + {長|ちょう} (chief, head). Refers to the person who is second in command to a {長|ちょう} (director/chief). The exact English equivalent varies by context: deputy director, vice-chief, assistant manager, etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事務次長|じむじちょう} (deputy secretary-general)
- {課長|かちょう}・{次長|じちょう}・{部長|ぶちょう} (section chief → deputy director → department head, typical hierarchy)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {副〜|ふく〜}: vice-/deputy- — a prefix used with titles ({副社長|ふくしゃちょう}, {副部長|ふくぶちょう}), often interchangeable in meaning
- {部長|ぶちょう}: department head — the position directly above {次長|じちょう}
